title: Problem Overview
content:
**Erdős Problem #476: The Erdős-Heilbronn Conjecture**

For a subset A of the finite field 𝔽ₚ, define the **restricted sumset**:
  A +̂ A = {a + b : a ≠ b ∈ A}

This excludes "diagonal" sums a + a = 2a.

**Question:** Is |A +̂ A| ≥ min(2|A| - 3, p)?

**Answer:** YES (da Silva-Hamidoune, 1994)
mathContext: The ordinary Cauchy-Davenport theorem gives |A + A| ≥ min(2|A| - 1, p). Excluding diagonals costs 2 elements.

title: Restricted Sumset Definition
content:
**restrictedSumset A:**

The set of all sums a + b where a and b are DISTINCT elements of A.

**Implementation:**
```lean
def restrictedSumset (A : Finset (ZMod p)) : Finset (ZMod p) :=
  (A.product A).filter (fun ab => ab.1 ≠ ab.2)
    |>.image (fun ab => ab.1 + ab.2)
```

Filter out pairs (a, a), then take sums.
mathContext: The notation A +̂ A is standard in additive combinatorics.

title: Ordinary Sumset Definition
content:
**sumset A:**

The ordinary sumset A + A includes ALL sums a + b, including a = b.

```lean
def sumset (A : Finset (ZMod p)) : Finset (ZMod p) :=
  (A.product A).image (fun ab => ab.1 + ab.2)
```

By Cauchy-Davenport: |A + A| ≥ min(2|A| - 1, p).
mathContext: Lean: `def sumset (A : Finset (ZMod p)) : Finset (ZMod p) :=`

title: Restricted Subset of Ordinary
content:
**restrictedSumset_subset_sumset:**

A +̂ A ⊆ A + A

Every sum of distinct elements is also a sum (possibly equal). The restricted sumset is always contained in the ordinary sumset.

title: Singleton Restricted Sumset
content:
**restrictedSumset_singleton:**

{a} +̂ {a} = ∅

A singleton has no pairs of distinct elements, so its restricted sumset is empty. This is the edge case where the bound 2|A| - 3 = -1 would be negative.

title: The Erdős-Heilbronn Bound
content:
**erdos_heilbronn_bound:**

For any A ⊆ 𝔽ₚ with |A| ≥ 2:
  |A +̂ A| ≥ min(2|A| - 3, p)

**erdos_476:**
The main theorem directly follows from this axiom.

This bound is TIGHT - arithmetic progressions achieve exactly 2|A| - 3 elements.
mathContext: The proof uses exterior algebra (Grassmann derivatives) or the polynomial method.

title: Da Silva-Hamidoune Theorem
content:
**da_silva_hamidoune (1994):**

The original proof uses **exterior algebra** over 𝔽ₚ.

**Key Idea:**
Consider the Grassmann (exterior) algebra ⋀(𝔽ₚⁿ). The k-th derivative of a polynomial relates to k-fold sums. By tracking dimensions in this algebra, one obtains the lower bound.

This approach connects combinatorics to advanced linear algebra.
mathContext: Grassmann derivatives generalize ordinary derivatives to wedge products.

title: Tightness via Arithmetic Progressions
content:
**arithmeticProgression:**

A = {a, a+d, a+2d, ..., a+(n-1)d} in 𝔽ₚ.

**AP_restrictedSumset:**
For this A with d ≠ 0:
  A +̂ A = {2a+d, 2a+2d, ..., 2a+(2n-3)d}

This has exactly 2n - 3 elements (when small enough).

So the bound min(2|A| - 3, p) is TIGHT - we cannot improve it.
mathContext: APs are the extremal examples for many sumset problems.

title: Comparison with Cauchy-Davenport
content:
**cauchy_davenport:**

For nonempty A, B ⊆ 𝔽ₚ:
  |A + B| ≥ min(|A| + |B| - 1, p)

**Comparison:**
- Ordinary: |A + A| ≥ min(2|A| - 1, p)
- Restricted: |A +̂ A| ≥ min(2|A| - 3, p)

The difference of 2 reflects the exclusion of diagonal sums.
mathContext: Cauchy-Davenport is fundamental in additive combinatorics, proved in 1813/1935.

title: The Polynomial Method
content:
**Combinatorial Nullstellensatz (Alon, 1999):**

A powerful tool: if a polynomial f has a leading monomial with nonzero coefficient, then f is nonzero on a sufficiently large grid.

**ANR Proof (1995):**
Alon, Nathanson, and Ruzsa gave an alternative proof of Erdős-Heilbronn using this method.

Construct f(x,y) = ∏_{c ∉ A+̂A} (x + y - c) and analyze its coefficients.
mathContext: The polynomial method is now central to additive combinatorics.

title: Generalization to r-Sums
content:
**restrictedSumsetR:**

The set of sums a₁ + a₂ + ... + aᵣ where all aᵢ are distinct elements of A.

**erdos_generalized:**
|r-fold restricted sumset| ≥ min(r|A| - r² + 1, p)

For r = 2: min(2|A| - 3, p) ✓

This generalization was also conjectured by Erdős and proved via the polynomial method.

title: Example: |A| = 2
content:
**card_two_case:**

If A = {a, b} with a ≠ b, then:
  A +̂ A = {a + b}

Exactly 1 element. The bound gives min(2·2 - 3, p) = min(1, p) = 1. ✓
mathContext: $If A = {a, b} with a ≠ b, then:$

title: Example: |A| = 3
content:
**card_three_lower_bound:**

For |A| = 3, the restricted sumset has at least 3 elements.

The bound gives min(2·3 - 3, p) = min(3, p) = 3 for p ≥ 3.

If A = {a, b, c}, then A +̂ A contains a+b, a+c, b+c (at least 3 elements).
mathContext: $For |A| = 3, the restricted sumset has at least 3 elements.$

title: Summary Theorem
content:
**erdos_476_summary:**

Combines the main results:
1. |A +̂ A| ≥ min(2|A| - 3, p) for all A with |A| ≥ 2
2. The bound is tight (achieved by arithmetic progressions)

The Erdős-Heilbronn conjecture is completely resolved.
mathContext: $1. |A +̂ A| ≥ min(2|A| - 3, p) for all A with |A| ≥ 2$
